text.p: These are the main stories in the Bosnian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Long-awaited summit between Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and chairman of Bosnian collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, begins in Split. Special U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard and architect of Bosnia's peace, Richard Holbrooke, are expected to attend.

- Preparations for the summit have been relatively smooth and there are only few disputes to be resolved in confidence between Tudjman and Izetbegovic, said Bosnian ambassador to Croatia, Kasim Trnka.
- Council of Ministers failed to agree on disputed citizenship law despite considerable efforts by office of the High representative and other international mediators.

- The main disputes surrounding the citizenship law are divergent interpretations of citizenship, relations between the entities and the central Bosnian state and dual citizenship, says Croat co-chairman of council, Neven Tomic.

- The shadow government has asked Moslem-Croat federation President Vladimir Soljic and Vice-President Ejup Ganic to resign due to their failure to prevent recent incidents in the central town of Jajce.
- Minimum level of pensions for August in the Moslem-Croat federation will be 8,000 dinars (80 German Marks).

- The federation government adopted a report on execution of the budget for the first half of the year. Total revenues for the six-month period were 272 million German marks ($151 million), 11 percent less than forecast.
- World Bank deputy director Saumya Mitra said education and transport projects which won financial support at the recent donors' conference are due to begin by late August.
- A unifed police force for the central canton in the Moslem-Croat federation should be established by August 11, according to an agreement reached on Tuesday.

- The state postal company says telephone links with the northern town of Banja Luka and Trebinje in the south were restored Tuesday midnight after a five-year interruption. The company announced telephone connections between the Moslem-Croat federation and Pale and other towns within Bosnia's Serb entity.

- The U.N. organisation for industrial development has launched a training programme worth $483,000 for managers of small companies which is aimed at attracting foreign investment. Business development centres will be opened in Bihac, Novi Travnik and Banja Luka. --Sarajevo newsroom +387 71 663 864
